AWSTemplateFormatVersion: '2010-09-09'
Description: Serverless Step Functions workflow that publishes custom events to a custom EventBridge event bus, with an EventBridge rule forwarding every event on that bus to a CloudWatch Logs log group for debugging.

Parameters:
  AppName:
    Type: String
    Default: eventflow
    MinLength: 1
    MaxLength: 40
    AllowedPattern: '[a-z0-9-]+'
    Description: Lowercase application name used as a prefix for resource names.
  Env:
    Type: String
    Default: dev
    AllowedValues:
      - dev
      - test
      - staging
      - prod
    Description: Deployment environment used as a name suffix.
  LogRetentionDays:
    Type: Number
    Default: 14
    AllowedValues:
      - 1
      - 3
      - 5
      - 7
      - 14
      - 30
      - 60
      - 90
      - 180
      - 365
    Description: Number of days to retain forwarded EventBridge debug events in CloudWatch Logs.

Resources:
  CustomEventBus:
    Type: AWS::Events::EventBus
    DeletionPolicy: Retain
    UpdateReplacePolicy: Retain
    Properties:
      Name: !Sub '${AppName}-${Env}-bus'

  EventDebugLogGroup:
    Type: AWS::Logs::LogGroup
    DeletionPolicy: Retain
    UpdateReplacePolicy: Retain
    Properties:
      LogGroupName: !Sub '/aws/events/${AppName}-${Env}-events'
      RetentionInDays: !Ref LogRetentionDays

  EventDebugLogResourcePolicy:
    Type: AWS::Logs::ResourcePolicy
    Properties:
      PolicyName: !Sub '${AppName}-${Env}-events-logs-policy'
      PolicyDocument: !Sub
        - |
          {
            "Version": "2012-10-17",
            "Statement": [
              {
                "Sid": "AllowEventBridgeToWriteLogs",
                "Effect": "Allow",
                "Principal": {
                  "Service": "events.amazonaws.com"
                },
                "Action": [
                  "logs:CreateLogStream",
                  "logs:PutLogEvents"
                ],
                "Resource": "${LogGroupArn}"
              }
            ]
          }
        - LogGroupArn: !GetAtt EventDebugLogGroup.Arn

  StateMachineRole:
    Type: AWS::IAM::Role
    Properties:
      RoleName: !Sub '${AppName}-${Env}-sfn-putevents-role'
      Description: Allows the Step Functions state machine to publish custom events to the application EventBridge event bus.
      AssumeRolePolicyDocument:
        Version: '2012-10-17'
        Statement:
          - Effect: Allow
            Principal:
              Service: states.amazonaws.com
            Action: sts:AssumeRole
      Policies:
        - PolicyName: PublishEventsToCustomBus
          PolicyDocument:
            Version: '2012-10-17'
            Statement:
              - Sid: AllowPutEventsOnCustomBus
                Effect: Allow
                Action: events:PutEvents
                Resource: !GetAtt CustomEventBus.Arn

  WorkflowStateMachine:
    Type: AWS::StepFunctions::StateMachine
    Properties:
      StateMachineName: !Sub '${AppName}-${Env}-workflow'
      StateMachineType: STANDARD
      RoleArn: !GetAtt StateMachineRole.Arn
      DefinitionString: !Sub
        - |
          {
            "Comment": "Publishes a custom event to the application EventBridge event bus.",
            "StartAt": "PublishCustomEvent",
            "States": {
              "PublishCustomEvent": {
                "Type": "Task",
                "Resource": "arn:${AWS::Partition}:states:::events:putEvents",
                "Parameters": {
                  "Entries": [
                    {
                      "EventBusName": "${EventBusArn}",
                      "Source": "com.${AppName}.${Env}.workflow",
                      "DetailType": "WorkflowEvent",
                      "Detail": {
                        "message": "Custom event emitted by the ${AppName}-${Env} state machine",
                        "app": "${AppName}",
                        "env": "${Env}"
                      }
                    }
                  ]
                },
                "End": true
              }
            }
          }
        - EventBusArn: !GetAtt CustomEventBus.Arn
          AppName: !Ref AppName
          Env: !Ref Env

  DebugForwardingRule:
    Type: AWS::Events::Rule
    Properties:
      Name: !Sub '${AppName}-${Env}-forward-all-to-logs'
      Description: Forwards every event published to the custom application event bus to a CloudWatch Logs log group for testing and debugging.
      EventBusName: !Ref CustomEventBus
      State: ENABLED
      EventPattern:
        source:
          - prefix: ''
      Targets:
        - Id: EventDebugLogTarget
          Arn: !GetAtt EventDebugLogGroup.Arn

Outputs:
  EventBusName:
    Description: Name of the custom EventBridge event bus.
    Value: !Ref CustomEventBus
  EventBusArn:
    Description: ARN of the custom EventBridge event bus.
    Value: !GetAtt CustomEventBus.Arn
  StateMachineArn:
    Description: ARN of the Step Functions state machine that publishes custom events.
    Value: !Ref WorkflowStateMachine
  LogGroupName:
    Description: Name of the CloudWatch Logs log group receiving forwarded events.
    Value: !Ref EventDebugLogGroup
  EventBridgeRuleArn:
    Description: ARN of the EventBridge rule that forwards all bus events to CloudWatch Logs.
    Value: !GetAtt DebugForwardingRule.Arn

AWSTemplateFormatVersion: '2010-09-09'
Description: >-
  Builds the AWS Cloud WAN global network and core network used for centralized
  outbound traffic inspection. The core network is created with multi-Region
  edge locations, 'production' and 'development' segments, an 'inspection'
  network function group, tag-based attachment policies and segment actions that
  steer all egress from both segments through the inspection VPC attachments.
  Tagging convention required by this policy: every inspection VPC attachment
  must carry the tag key 'domain' with value 'inspection', every production
  workload VPC attachment must carry 'domain=production' and every development
  workload VPC attachment must carry 'domain=development'. The inspection VPCs
  themselves and their attachments are created by a separate stack that uses the
  core network outputs below.

Parameters:
  ProjectName:
    Type: String
    Default: cloudwan-inspection
    MinLength: 3
    MaxLength: 40
    AllowedPattern: '^[a-zA-Z0-9-]+$'
    ConstraintDescription: Must contain only letters, numbers and hyphens.
    Description: >-
      Project identifier applied to the 'Project' tag of every resource in this
      stack, to resource names and to the stack export names.

  Environment:
    Type: String
    Default: shared
    MinLength: 3
    MaxLength: 20
    AllowedPattern: '^[a-z0-9-]+$'
    ConstraintDescription: Must contain only lowercase letters, numbers and hyphens.
    Description: >-
      Environment label applied to the 'Environment' tag of every resource in
      this stack (for example 'shared', 'prod' or 'nonprod').

  EdgeRegion:
    Type: String
    Default: us-west-2
    AllowedPattern: '^[a-z]{2}(-gov)?-[a-z]+-\d$'
    ConstraintDescription: Must be a valid AWS Region name such as us-west-2.
    Description: >-
      Secondary AWS Region used for the second Cloud WAN core network edge
      location. The primary edge location is always the Region in which this
      stack is deployed.

Resources:

  GlobalNetwork:
    Type: AWS::NetworkManager::GlobalNetwork
    Properties:
      Description: !Sub 'Cloud WAN global network for ${ProjectName} centralized outbound traffic inspection'
      Tags:
        - Key: Name
          Value: !Sub '${ProjectName}-global-network'
        - Key: Environment
          Value: !Ref Environment
        - Key: Project
          Value: !Ref ProjectName

  CoreNetwork:
    Type: AWS::NetworkManager::CoreNetwork
    Properties:
      GlobalNetworkId: !Ref GlobalNetwork
      Description: !Sub '${ProjectName} core network - production and development segments inspected by the inspection network function group'
      PolicyDocument:
        version: '2021.12'
        core-network-configuration:
          asn-ranges:
            - '64512-65534'
          edge-locations:
            - location: !Ref 'AWS::Region'
              asn: 64512
              inside-cidr-blocks:
                - 10.200.0.0/16
              vpn-ecmp-support: true
            - location: !Ref EdgeRegion
              asn: 64513
              inside-cidr-blocks:
                - 10.201.0.0/16
              vpn-ecmp-support: true
        segments:
          - name: production
            description: Production workloads. Attachments cannot reach each other and require no manual acceptance.
            isolate-attachments: true
            require-attachment-acceptance: false
          - name: development
            description: Development workloads. Attachments require no manual acceptance and route back to the inspection network function group.
            require-attachment-acceptance: false
        network-function-groups:
          - name: inspection
            description: Inspection VPC attachments that provide centralized outbound traffic inspection for the production and development segments.
            require-attachment-acceptance: false
        attachment-policies:
          - rule-number: 100
            description: Associate VPC attachments tagged domain=inspection with the inspection network function group.
            condition:
              type: and
              expressions:
                - type: tag-value
                  key: domain
                  value: inspection
            action:
              association-method: constant
              network-function-group: inspection
              require-acceptance: false
          - rule-number: 200
            description: Associate VPC attachments tagged domain=production with the production segment.
            condition:
              type: and
              expressions:
                - type: tag-value
                  key: domain
                  value: production
            action:
              association-method: tag
              tag-value-of-key: domain
              require-acceptance: false
          - rule-number: 300
            description: Associate VPC attachments tagged domain=development with the development segment.
            condition:
              type: and
              expressions:
                - type: tag-value
                  key: domain
                  value: development
            action:
              association-method: tag
              tag-value-of-key: domain
              require-acceptance: false
        segment-actions:
          - action: send-via
            segment: production
            mode: single-hop
            via:
              network-function-group: inspection
          - action: send-via
            segment: development
            mode: single-hop
            via:
              network-function-group: inspection
      Tags:
        - Key: Name
          Value: !Sub '${ProjectName}-core-network'
        - Key: Environment
          Value: !Ref Environment
        - Key: Project
          Value: !Ref ProjectName

Outputs:

  GlobalNetworkId:
    Description: ID of the Cloud WAN global network.
    Value: !Ref GlobalNetwork
    Export:
      Name: !Sub '${ProjectName}-${Environment}-cloudwan-global-network-id'

  CoreNetworkId:
    Description: ID of the Cloud WAN core network.
    Value: !Ref CoreNetwork
    Export:
      Name: !Sub '${ProjectName}-${Environment}-cloudwan-core-network-id'

  CoreNetworkArn:
    Description: ARN of the Cloud WAN core network used to create VPC attachments.
    Value: !GetAtt CoreNetwork.CoreNetworkArn
    Export:
      Name: !Sub '${ProjectName}-${Environment}-cloudwan-core-network-arn'
deploy_logs: ["Creating stack 'iac-god-eval-6b6505b8' on localstack", 'iac-god-eval-6b6505b8: CREATE_IN_PROGRESS - N/A', 'GlobalNetwork: CREATE_IN_PROGRESS - N/A', 'GlobalNetwork: CREATE_COMPLETE - Resource type AWS::NetworkManager::GlobalNetwork is not supported but was deployed as a fallback', 'CoreNetwork: CREATE_IN_PROGRESS - N/A', 'CoreNetwork: CREATE_COMPLETE - Resource type AWS::NetworkManager::CoreNetwork is not supported but was deployed as a fallback', 'iac-god-eval-6b6505b8: CREATE_COMPLETE - N/A']
deploy_completed_resources: GlobalNetwork | CoreNetwork

AWSTemplateFormatVersion: '2010-09-09'
Description: Test resources for validating the CloudFormation template approval workflow - a WaitConditionHandle carrying greeting and timestamp metadata plus an SSM parameter holding the approval workflow test data.

Parameters:
  Name:
    Type: String
    Default: World
    Description: Name used in the SSM parameter path and in the greeting message.
  CustomMessage:
    Type: String
    Default: Hello from CloudFormation
    Description: Custom message stored in the approval workflow SSM parameter value.

Resources:

  DeploymentTimestampFunctionRole:
    Type: AWS::IAM::Role
    Properties:
      Description: Execution role for the deployment timestamp custom resource function.
      AssumeRolePolicyDocument:
        Version: '2012-10-17'
        Statement:
          - Effect: Allow
            Principal:
              Service: lambda.amazonaws.com
            Action: sts:AssumeRole
      Policies:
        - PolicyName: WriteFunctionLogs
          PolicyDocument:
            Version: '2012-10-17'
            Statement:
              - Effect: Allow
                Action:
                  - logs:CreateLogGroup
                  - logs:CreateLogStream
                  - logs:PutLogEvents
                Resource: !Sub 'arn:${AWS::Partition}:logs:${AWS::Region}:${AWS::AccountId}:log-group:/aws/lambda/*'

  DeploymentTimestampFunction:
    Type: AWS::Lambda::Function
    Properties:
      Description: Signals a deployment timestamp back to CloudFormation for the approval workflow test metadata.
      Runtime: python3.12
      Handler: index.handler
      Role: !GetAtt DeploymentTimestampFunctionRole.Arn
      Timeout: 30
      Code:
        ZipFile: |
          import json
          import urllib.request
          from datetime import datetime, timezone


          def send_response(event, status, reason, data=None):
              body = {
                  'Status': status,
                  'Reason': reason,
                  'PhysicalResourceId': event.get('PhysicalResourceId', 'deployment-timestamp'),
                  'StackId': event.get('StackId', ''),
                  'RequestId': event.get('RequestId', ''),
                  'LogicalResourceId': event.get('LogicalResourceId', ''),
                  'Data': data or {},
              }
              payload = json.dumps(body).encode('utf-8')
              request = urllib.request.Request(
                  event['ResponseURL'],
                  data=payload,
                  method='PUT',
                  headers={'Content-Type': 'application/json'},
              )
              urllib.request.urlopen(request)


          def handler(event, context):
              request_type = event.get('RequestType')
              try:
                  data = {
                      'Timestamp': datetime.now(timezone.utc).strftime('%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ')
                  }
                  send_response(
                      event,
                      'SUCCESS',
                      'Deployment timestamp resolved for {} request.'.format(request_type or 'UNKNOWN'),
                      data,
                  )
              except Exception as error:
                  try:
                      send_response(
                          event,
                          'FAILED',
                          'Deployment timestamp handler failed: {}'.format(error),
                      )
                  except Exception:
                      pass

  DeploymentTimestampFunctionPermission:
    Type: AWS::Lambda::Permission
    Properties:
      Action: lambda:InvokeFunction
      FunctionName: !Ref DeploymentTimestampFunction
      Principal: cloudformation.amazonaws.com
      SourceAccount: !Ref AWS::AccountId
      SourceArn: !Sub 'arn:${AWS::Partition}:cloudformation:${AWS::Region}:${AWS::AccountId}:stack/${AWS::StackName}/*'

  DeploymentTimestamp:
    Type: AWS::CloudFormation::CustomResource
    Properties:
      ServiceToken: !GetAtt DeploymentTimestampFunction.Arn
      ServiceTimeout: 60

  ApprovalWorkflowTestHandle:
    Type: AWS::CloudFormation::WaitConditionHandle
    Metadata:
      greeting: !Sub 'Hello, ${Name}!'
      timestamp: !GetAtt DeploymentTimestamp.Timestamp

  ApprovalTestParameter:
    Type: AWS::SSM::Parameter
    DeletionPolicy: Retain
    UpdateReplacePolicy: Retain
    Properties:
      Name: !Sub '/iidy/template-approval/test/${Name}'
      Type: String
      Value: !Sub '{"stackName": "${AWS::StackName}", "stackId": "${AWS::StackId}", "message": "${CustomMessage}", "approvalWorkflowEnabled": true}'

Outputs:
  ParameterName:
    Description: Name of the SSM parameter that stores the approval workflow test data.
    Value: !Ref ApprovalTestParameter
  Greeting:
    Description: Greeting message used by the approval workflow test.
    Value: !Sub 'Hello, ${Name}!'

AWSTemplateFormatVersion: '2010-09-09'
Description: Provisions a DynamoDB table and a Step Functions standard workflow that writes and reads an item for testing.

Parameters:
  TableName:
    Type: String
    Default: my-table
    Description: Name of the DynamoDB table to create and use in the Step Functions workflow.
    AllowedPattern: '[a-zA-Z0-9_.-]+'
    MinLength: 3
    MaxLength: 255

Resources:
  DynamoDBTable:
    Type: AWS::DynamoDB::Table
    DeletionPolicy: Retain
    UpdateReplacePolicy: Retain
    Properties:
      TableName: !Ref TableName
      BillingMode: PAY_PER_REQUEST
      AttributeDefinitions:
        - AttributeName: id
          AttributeType: S
      KeySchema:
        - AttributeName: id
          KeyType: HASH

  StepFunctionsExecutionRole:
    Type: AWS::IAM::Role
    Properties:
      AssumeRolePolicyDocument:
        Version: '2012-10-17'
        Statement:
          - Effect: Allow
            Principal:
              Service: states.amazonaws.com
            Action: sts:AssumeRole
      Policies:
        - PolicyName: DynamoDBAccess
          PolicyDocument:
            Version: '2012-10-17'
            Statement:
              - Effect: Allow
                Action:
                  - dynamodb:PutItem
                  - dynamodb:GetItem
                Resource:
                  - !GetAtt DynamoDBTable.Arn
                  - !Sub '${DynamoDBTable.Arn}/*'

  TestStateMachine:
    Type: AWS::StepFunctions::StateMachine
    Properties:
      StateMachineType: STANDARD
      RoleArn: !GetAtt StepFunctionsExecutionRole.Arn
      DefinitionString: !Sub
        - |
          {
            "Comment": "Test workflow that writes and reads a DynamoDB item.",
            "StartAt": "PutItem",
            "States": {
              "PutItem": {
                "Type": "Task",
                "Resource": "arn:aws:states:::dynamodb:putItem",
                "Parameters": {
                  "TableName": "${TableName}",
                  "Item": {
                    "id": {
                      "S.$": "$.id"
                    },
                    "description": {
                      "S.$": "States.Format('Item {}', $.name)"
                    }
                  }
                },
                "ResultPath": null,
                "Next": "GetItem",
                "Retry": [
                  {
                    "ErrorEquals": [
                      "DynamoDB.ProvisionedThroughputExceededException",
                      "DynamoDB.ThrottlingException",
                      "DynamoDB.RequestLimitExceeded"
                    ],
                    "IntervalSeconds": 1,
                    "MaxAttempts": 3,
                    "BackoffRate": 2.0
                  }
                ]
              },
              "GetItem": {
                "Type": "Task",
                "Resource": "arn:aws:states:::dynamodb:getItem",
                "Parameters": {
                  "TableName": "${TableName}",
                  "Key": {
                    "id": {
                      "S.$": "$.id"
                    }
                  }
                },
                "OutputPath": "$.Item",
                "End": true,
                "Retry": [
                  {
                    "ErrorEquals": [
                      "DynamoDB.ProvisionedThroughputExceededException",
                      "DynamoDB.ThrottlingException",
                      "DynamoDB.RequestLimitExceeded"
                    ],
                    "IntervalSeconds": 1,
                    "MaxAttempts": 3,
                    "BackoffRate": 2.0
                  }
                ]
              }
            }
          }
        - TableName: !Ref TableName

Outputs:
  DynamoDBTableName:
    Description: Name of the DynamoDB table.
    Value: !Ref DynamoDBTable
  StateMachineArn:
    Description: ARN of the Step Functions state machine.
    Value: !Ref TestStateMachine
  StateMachineName:
    Description: Name of the Step Functions state machine.
    Value: !GetAtt TestStateMachine.Name
deploy_logs: ["Creating stack 'iac-god-eval-b8aacbcd' on localstack", 'iac-god-eval-b8aacbcd: CREATE_IN_PROGRESS - N/A', 'DynamoDBTable: CREATE_IN_PROGRESS - N/A', 'DynamoDBTable: CREATE_COMPLETE - N/A', 'StepFunctionsExecutionRole: CREATE_IN_PROGRESS - N/A', 'StepFunctionsExecutionRole: CREATE_COMPLETE - N/A', 'TestStateMachine: CREATE_IN_PROGRESS - N/A', 'TestStateMachine: CREATE_COMPLETE - N/A', 'iac-god-eval-b8aacbcd: CREATE_COMPLETE - N/A']

AWSTemplateFormatVersion: '2010-09-09'
Description: >-
  AWS DevOps Agent Space with IAM roles for the AWS DevOps Agent service and the
  DevOps Agent operator application. Creates the agent space and two IAM roles
  whose trust policies allow aidevops.amazonaws.com to assume them only for agent
  spaces in this account (aws:SourceAccount and aws:SourceArn conditions), and
  grants each role its permissions through in-template inline policies so no
  external managed-policy ARNs are required.

Resources:

  DevOpsAgentSpace:
    Type: AWS::DevOpsAgent::AgentSpace
    DeletionPolicy: Retain
    UpdateReplacePolicy: Retain
    Properties:
      Name: DevOpsAgentSpace
      Description: Primary AWS DevOps Agent space for this account.
      Tags:
        - Key: Name
          Value: DevOpsAgentSpace
        - Key: Environment
          Value: Production

  # NOTE: No separate CloudFormation resource type is published for registering this
  # account as the primary monitoring account for the agent space (no confirmed type
  # exists in the AWS CloudFormation resource specification for the DevOps Agent
  # namespace). The account association is therefore not modeled as a standalone
  # resource here; it must be configured through the AgentSpace resource's own
  # supported properties or outside of this template.

  DevOpsAgentServiceRole:
    Type: AWS::IAM::Role
    DeletionPolicy: Retain
    UpdateReplacePolicy: Retain
    Properties:
      RoleName: DevOpsAgentServiceRole
      Description: Role assumed by the AWS DevOps Agent service to operate the agent space.
      AssumeRolePolicyDocument:
        Version: '2012-10-17'
        Statement:
          - Sid: AllowDevOpsAgentServiceAssumeRole
            Effect: Allow
            Principal:
              Service: aidevops.amazonaws.com
            Action: sts:AssumeRole
            Condition:
              StringEquals:
                aws:SourceAccount: !Ref 'AWS::AccountId'
                aws:SourceArn: !GetAtt DevOpsAgentSpace.Arn
      Policies:
        - PolicyName: AllowCreateDevOpsAgentServiceLinkedRole
          PolicyDocument:
            Version: '2012-10-17'
            Statement:
              - Sid: AllowCreateServiceLinkedRole
                Effect: Allow
                Action: iam:CreateServiceLinkedRole
                Resource: !Sub 'arn:${AWS::Partition}:iam::${AWS::AccountId}:role/aws-service-role/aidevops.amazonaws.com/*'
                Condition:
                  StringEquals:
                    iam:AWSServiceName: aidevops.amazonaws.com
        - PolicyName: DevOpsAgentServiceReadAccess
          PolicyDocument:
            Version: '2012-10-17'
            Statement:
              - Sid: AllowDescribeResources
                Effect: Allow
                Action:
                  - cloudwatch:DescribeAlarms
                  - cloudwatch:GetMetricData
                  - cloudwatch:GetMetricStatistics
                  - cloudwatch:ListMetrics
                  - logs:DescribeLogGroups
                  - logs:DescribeLogStreams
                  - logs:FilterLogEvents
                  - logs:GetLogEvents
                  - ec2:DescribeInstances
                  - ec2:DescribeInstanceStatus
                  - ecs:DescribeClusters
                  - ecs:DescribeServices
                  - ecs:ListClusters
                  - ecs:ListServices
                  - eks:DescribeCluster
                  - eks:ListClusters
                  - lambda:GetFunction
                  - lambda:ListFunctions
                  - rds:DescribeDBInstances
                  - dynamodb:DescribeTable
                  - dynamodb:ListTables
                  - events:DescribeRule
                  - events:ListRules
                  - health:DescribeEvents
                  - health:DescribeEventDetails
                  - health:DescribeAffectedEntities
                  - tag:GetResources
                Resource: '*'
        - PolicyName: AllowCreateDevOpsAgentOAuthToken
          PolicyDocument:
            Version: '2012-10-17'
            Statement:
              - Sid: AllowAssumeRolesForInvestigation
                Effect: Allow
                Action: sts:AssumeRole
                Resource: !GetAtt DevOpsAgentOperatorAppRole.Arn
      Tags:
        - Key: Name
          Value: DevOpsAgentServiceRole
        - Key: Environment
          Value: Production

  DevOpsAgentOperatorAppRole:
    Type: AWS::IAM::Role
    DeletionPolicy: Retain
    UpdateReplacePolicy: Retain
    Properties:
      RoleName: DevOpsAgentOperatorAppRole
      Description: Role assumed by the AWS DevOps Agent operator application.
      AssumeRolePolicyDocument:
        Version: '2012-10-17'
        Statement:
          - Sid: AllowDevOpsAgentOperatorAppAssumeRole
            Effect: Allow
            Principal:
              Service: aidevops.amazonaws.com
            Action: sts:AssumeRole
            Condition:
              StringEquals:
                aws:SourceAccount: !Ref 'AWS::AccountId'
                aws:SourceArn: !GetAtt DevOpsAgentSpace.Arn
      Policies:
        - PolicyName: DevOpsAgentOperatorAppPermissions
          PolicyDocument:
            Version: '2012-10-17'
            Statement:
              - Sid: AllowDescribeResources
                Effect: Allow
                Action:
                  - cloudwatch:DescribeAlarms

AWSTemplateFormatVersion: '2010-09-09'

Description: >
  Lambda-based CI/CD deployment environment using AWS CodeDeploy blue-green
  traffic shifting with automated validation. This template is fully self-contained
  for a greenfield account: it creates every IAM role, Lambda function, Lambda
  version/alias, secret, CodeDeploy application and canary deployment group it
  depends on. No external VPC, subnet, AMI, bucket, SSM parameter or secret is
  referenced.

  NOTE: The AppSpec revision supplied at deployment time must declare the lifecycle
  hooks named "BeforeAllowTraffic" and "AfterAllowTraffic" (hooks section) and must
  target the "live" alias of the main function; those names match the resources below.

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Parameters (optional, non-infrastructure only; every parameter is referenced)
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
Parameters:
  Environment:
    Type: String
    Description: Logical environment name used for tagging and function configuration.
    Default: dev
    AllowedValues:
      - dev
      - test
      - staging
      - prod
    ConstraintDescription: Must be one of dev, test, staging or prod.

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Resources
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
Resources:

  # -------------------------------------------------------------------------
  # Runtime secret (created inline - no external secret is referenced)
  # -------------------------------------------------------------------------
  ApplicationSecret:
    Type: AWS::SecretsManager::Secret
    DeletionPolicy: Retain
    UpdateReplacePolicy: Retain
    Properties:
      Name: !Sub '${AWS::StackName}/app-secret'
      Description: Runtime secret for the main deployment Lambda function. Generated by CloudFormation.
      GenerateSecretString:
        SecretStringTemplate: '{"username":"appuser"}'
        GenerateStringKey: password
        PasswordLength: 32
        ExcludePunctuation: true
      Tags:
        - Key: Environment
          Value: !Ref Environment

  # -------------------------------------------------------------------------
  # IAM execution role for the main Lambda function
  # (AWS managed AWSLambdaBasicExecutionRole -> CloudWatch Logs)
  # -------------------------------------------------------------------------
  MainFunctionRole:
    Type: AWS::IAM::Role
    Properties:
      RoleName: !Sub '${AWS::StackName}-main-lambda-role'
      Description: Execution role for the main blue/green deployment Lambda function.
      AssumeRolePolicyDocument:
        Version: '2012-10-17'
        Statement:
          - Effect: Allow
            Principal:
              Service: lambda.amazonaws.com
            Action: sts:AssumeRole
      ManagedPolicyArns:
        - !Sub 'arn:${AWS::Partition}:iam::aws:policy/service-role/AWSLambdaBasicExecutionRole'
      Policies:
        - PolicyName: ReadApplicationSecret
          PolicyDocument:
            Version: '2012-10-17'
            Statement:
              - Effect: Allow
                Action:
                  - secretsmanager:GetSecretValue
                  - secretsmanager:DescribeSecret
                Resource: !Ref ApplicationSecret
      Tags:
        - Key: Environment
          Value: !Ref Environment

  # -------------------------------------------------------------------------
  # Main Lambda function, immutable version and live alias
  # -------------------------------------------------------------------------
  MainFunction:
    Type: AWS::Lambda::Function
    Properties:
      FunctionName: !Sub '${AWS::StackName}-main'
      Description: Main application function deployed via CodeDeploy blue-green traffic shifting.
      Runtime: python3.12
      Handler: index.handler
      Role: !GetAtt MainFunctionRole.Arn
      Timeout: 15
      MemorySize: 256
      Environment:
        Variables:
          ENVIRONMENT: !Ref Environment
          LOG_LEVEL: INFO
          # Secret value is never embedded; only the ARN is passed to the function.
          SECRET_ARN: !Ref ApplicationSecret
          APPLICATION_NAME: !Ref CodeDeployApplication
      Code:
        ZipFile: |
          import json
          import os


          def handler(event, context):
              return {
                  "statusCode": 200,
                  "environment": os.environ.get("ENVIRONMENT", "unknown"),
                  "logLevel": os.environ.get("LOG_LEVEL", "INFO"),
                  "application": os.environ.get("APPLICATION_NAME", "unknown"),
                  "secretConfigured": bool(os.environ.get("SECRET_ARN")),
                  "body": json.dumps({"message": "Hello from the blue/green target"}),
              }
      Tags:
        - Key: Environment
          Value: !Ref Environment

  MainFunctionVersion:
    Type: AWS::Lambda::Version
    DeletionPolicy: Retain
    UpdateReplacePolicy: Retain
    Properties:
      FunctionName: !Ref MainFunction
      Description: !Sub 'Immutable version of ${MainFunction} used for CodeDeploy traffic shifting.'

  MainFunctionAlias:
    Type: AWS::Lambda::Alias
    Properties:
      Name: live
      Description: Live alias whose RoutingConfig is managed by CodeDeploy during traffic shifting.
      FunctionName: !Ref MainFunction
      FunctionVersion: !GetAtt MainFunctionVersion.Version
      # Note: the immutable version ARN is available via !Ref MainFunctionVersion (Ref returns the ARN).
      # CodeDeploy shifts traffic between versions by updating this alias's RoutingConfig.

  # -------------------------------------------------------------------------
  # Shared execution role for the lifecycle hook validation functions
  # -------------------------------------------------------------------------
  HookFunctionRole:
    Type: AWS::IAM::Role
    Properties:
      RoleName: !Sub '${AWS::StackName}-hook-lambda-role'
      Description: Shared execution role for CodeDeploy lifecycle hook validation functions.
      AssumeRolePolicyDocument:
        Version: '2012-10-17'
        Statement:
          - Effect: Allow
            Principal:
              Service: lambda.amazonaws.com
            Action: sts:AssumeRole
      ManagedPolicyArns:
        - !Sub 'arn:${AWS::Partition}:iam::aws:policy/service-role/AWSLambdaBasicExecutionRole'
      Policies:
        - PolicyName: ReportLifecycleEventHookStatus
          PolicyDocument:
            Version: '2012-10-17'
            Statement:
              - Effect: Allow
                Action:
                  - codedeploy:PutLifecycleEventHookExecutionStatus
                Resource: !Sub
                  - 'arn:${AWS::Partition}:codedeploy:${AWS::Region}:${AWS::AccountId}:deploymentgroup:${AppName}/${DgName}'
                  - AppName: !Ref CodeDeployApplication
                    # Literal string (not !Ref) to avoid a dependency cycle with the
                    # deployment group below, which DependsOn this role.
                    DgName: !Sub '${AWS::StackName}-dg'
      Tags:
        - Key: Environment
          Value: !Ref Environment

  # -------------------------------------------------------------------------
  # Lifecycle hook validation functions
  # Inline ZipFile code is packaged as index.py, so the handler is index.handler
  # for both hooks; they are distinct functions reporting distinct hook names.
  # -------------------------------------------------------------------------
  BeforeAllowTrafficHook:
    Type: AWS::Lambda::Function
    Properties:
      FunctionName: !Sub '${AWS::StackName}-before-allow-traffic'
      Description: Validation hook executed during CodeDeploy BeforeAllowTraffic.
      Runtime: python3.12
      Handler: index.handler
      Role: !GetAtt HookFunctionRole.Arn
      Timeout: 30
      MemorySize: 128
      Environment:
        Variables:
          HOOK_NAME: BeforeAllowTraffic
          ENVIRONMENT: !Ref Environment
          APPLICATION_NAME: !Ref CodeDeployApplication
          DEPLOYMENT_GROUP_NAME: !Sub '${AWS::StackName}-dg'
      Code:
        ZipFile: |
          import os
          import boto3

          codedeploy = boto3.client("codedeploy")


          def handler(event, context):
              codedeploy.put_lifecycle_event_hook_execution_status(
                  deploymentId=event["DeploymentId"],
                  lifecycleEventHookExecutionId=event["LifecycleEventHookExecutionId"],
                  status="Succeeded",
              )
              return {
                  "hook": os.environ.get("HOOK_NAME", "BeforeAllowTraffic"),
                  "application": os.environ.get("APPLICATION_NAME"),
                  "deploymentGroup": os.environ.get("DEPLOYMENT_GROUP_NAME"),
                  "status": "Succeeded",
              }
      Tags:
        - Key: Environment
          Value: !Ref Environment

  AfterAllowTrafficHook:
    Type: AWS::Lambda::Function
    Properties:
      FunctionName: !Sub '${AWS::StackName}-after-allow-traffic'
      Description: Validation hook executed during CodeDeploy AfterAllowTraffic.
      Runtime: python3.12
      Handler: index.handler
      Role: !GetAtt HookFunctionRole.Arn
      Timeout: 30
      MemorySize: 128
      Environment:
        Variables:
          HOOK_NAME: AfterAllowTraffic
          ENVIRONMENT: !Ref Environment
          APPLICATION_NAME: !Ref CodeDeployApplication
          DEPLOYMENT_GROUP_NAME: !Sub '${AWS::StackName}-dg'
      Code:
        ZipFile: |
          import os
          import boto3

          codedeploy = boto3.client("codedeploy")


          def handler(event, context):
              codedeploy.put_lifecycle_event_hook_execution_status(
                  deploymentId=event["DeploymentId"],
                  lifecycleEventHookExecutionId=event["LifecycleEventHookExecutionId"],
                  status="Succeeded",
              )
              return {
                  "hook": os.environ.get("HOOK_NAME", "AfterAllowTraffic"),
                  "application": os.environ.get("APPLICATION_NAME"),
                  "deploymentGroup": os.environ.get("DEPLOYMENT_GROUP_NAME"),
                  "status": "Succeeded",
              }
      Tags:
        - Key: Environment
          Value: !Ref Environment

  # -------------------------------------------------------------------------
  # CodeDeploy application and Lambda blue/green deployment group
  # -------------------------------------------------------------------------
  CodeDeployApplication:
    Type: AWS::CodeDeploy::Application
    Properties:
      ApplicationName: !Sub '${AWS::StackName}-app'
      ComputePlatform: Lambda
      Tags:
        - Key: Environment
          Value: !Ref Environment

  CodeDeployServiceRole:
    Type: AWS::IAM::Role
    Properties:
      RoleName: !Sub '${AWS::StackName}-codedeploy-role'
      Description: Service role assumed by CodeDeploy to manage Lambda traffic shifting.
      AssumeRolePolicyDocument:
        Version: '2012-10-17'
        Statement:
          - Effect: Allow
            Principal:
              Service: codedeploy.amazonaws.com
            Action: sts:AssumeRole
      ManagedPolicyArns:
        - !Sub 'arn:${AWS::Partition}:iam::aws:policy/service-role/AWSCodeDeployRoleForLambda'
      Tags:
        - Key: Environment
          Value: !Ref Environment

  CodeDeployDeploymentGroup:
    Type: AWS::CodeDeploy::DeploymentGroup
    # Genuine ordering need: the hook execution permissions must exist before the
    # deployment group can invoke the hooks. This does not create a cycle because
    # the hook role references the deployment group by name string, not by !Ref.
    DependsOn:
      - HookFunctionRole
      - BeforeAllowTrafficHook
      - AfterAllowTrafficHook
    Properties:
      ApplicationName: !Ref CodeDeployApplication
      DeploymentGroupName: !Sub '${AWS::StackName}-dg'
      ServiceRoleArn: !GetAtt CodeDeployServiceRole.Arn
      DeploymentStyle:
        DeploymentType: BLUE_GREEN
        DeploymentOption: WITH_TRAFFIC_CONTROL
      DeploymentConfigName: CodeDeployDefault.LambdaCanary10Percent5Minutes
      AutoRollbackConfiguration:
        Enabled: true
        Events:
          - DEPLOYMENT_FAILURE
          - DEPLOYMENT_STOP_ON_ALARM
          - DEPLOYMENT_STOP_ON_REQUEST
      # The targeted Lambda alias ("live") is not a property of the deployment
      # group; it is supplied in the AppSpec revision at deployment time
      # (resources -> LambdaFunctionAlias). No unverified resource type is used.
      Tags:
        - Key: Environment
          Value: !Ref Environment

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Outputs (no hardcoded names/ARNs - derived from the created resources)
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
Outputs:
  MainFunctionArn:
    Description: ARN of the main deployment Lambda function.
    Value: !GetAtt MainFunction.Arn

  MainFunctionAliasArn:
    Description: ARN of the live Lambda alias targeted by CodeDeploy traffic shifting.
    Value: !Ref MainFunctionAlias

  MainFunctionVersionArn:
    Description: ARN of the published immutable Lambda version used for blue/green shifting.
    Value: !Ref MainFunctionVersion

  CodeDeployApplicationName:
    Description: Name of the CodeDeploy application.
    Value: !Ref CodeDeployApplication

  CodeDeployDeploymentGroupName:
    Description: Name of the CodeDeploy deployment group.
    Value: !Ref CodeDeployDeploymentGroup

  CodeDeployServiceRoleArn:
    Description: ARN of the CodeDeploy service role used by the deployment group.
    Value: !GetAtt CodeDeployServiceRole.Arn

Description: >-
  AWS IVS live streaming channel and stream key. Creates an Amazon Interactive
  Video Service channel with a configurable latency mode, channel type and
  authorization flag, plus a service-generated stream key bound to that channel.

  referenced.

Parameters:
  LatencyMode:
    Type: String
    Default: LOW
    AllowedValues:
      - LOW
      - NORMAL
    Description: >-
      Channel latency mode. LOW enables low-latency ingest and playback (sub-3
      second); NORMAL uses the standard RTMPS ingest with higher latency.

  ChannelType:
    Type: String
    Default: STANDARD
    AllowedValues:
      - STANDARD
      - BASIC
      - ADVANCED
    Description: >-
      IVS channel type. STANDARD supports multiple qualities up to 1080p, BASIC
      is limited to 480p, ADVANCED supports up to 1080p60 with higher bitrates.

  Authorized:
    Type: String
    Default: 'false'
    AllowedValues:
      - 'true'
      - 'false'
    Description: >-
      Whether the channel requires an authorization token for playback. String
      values are used because CloudFormation has no Boolean parameter type; the
      value is passed directly to the channel's Boolean Authorized property.

  EnvironmentTag:
    Type: String
    Default: dev
    Description: Environment name applied to the channel name and resource tags.

  CustomTagKey:
    Type: String
    Default: Owner
    Description: Key of the custom tag applied to the channel and the stream key.

  CustomTagValue:
    Type: String
    Default: platform-team
    Description: >-
      Value of the custom tag applied to the channel and the stream key, used
      for ownership and cost allocation tracking.

Resources:
  IVSChannel:
    Type: AWS::IVS::Channel
    Properties:
      Name: !Sub 'IVS-${EnvironmentTag}-channel'
      Authorized: !Ref Authorized
      LatencyMode: !Ref LatencyMode
      Type: !Ref ChannelType
      Tags:
        - Key: Environment
          Value: !Ref EnvironmentTag
        - Key: !Ref CustomTagKey
          Value: !Ref CustomTagValue

  IVSStreamKey:
    Type: AWS::IVS::StreamKey
    Properties:
      ChannelArn: !Ref IVSChannel
      Tags:
        - Key: Environment
          Value: !Ref EnvironmentTag
        - Key: !Ref CustomTagKey
          Value: !Ref CustomTagValue

Outputs:
  IngestEndpoint:
    Description: RTMPS ingest endpoint URL to which the streaming encoder publishes.
    Value: !GetAtt IVSChannel.IngestEndpoint

  PlaybackUrl:
    Description: Public playback URL for viewers to watch the live stream.
    Value: !GetAtt IVSChannel.PlaybackUrl

  StreamKeyValue:
    Description: >-
      Service-generated IVS stream key value used to authenticate the broadcast.
      Treat this value as a sensitive credential: it is visible in the stack's
      Outputs tab and in describe-stacks API responses, so access to the
      CloudFormation console and API must be restricted accordingly.
    Value: !GetAtt IVSStreamKey.Value

AWSTemplateFormatVersion: '2010-09-09'
Description: Provisions PCI-DSS remediation prerequisites for AWS Config Conformance Packs - the shared IAM automation assume-role (pciautomationassumerole plus the deployment region) and four custom SSM Automation documents that Conformance Pack RemediationConfiguration actions invoke to restrict the VPC default security group, delete unused security groups, release unassociated Elastic IP addresses, and set Auto Scaling group ELB health checks with a 300 second grace period. Only confirmed resource types are used (AWS::IAM::Role and AWS::SSM::Document). No Conditions are declared and no resource carries a Condition attribute, so every resource is created unconditionally. Config RemediationConfiguration bindings live in the Conformance Pack stack that consumes this template's outputs.
Resources:
  PCIAutomationAssumeRole:
    Type: AWS::IAM::Role
    DeletionPolicy: Retain
    UpdateReplacePolicy: Retain
    Properties:
      RoleName:
        Fn::Sub: 'pciautomationassumerole${AWS::Region}'
      Description: Assumed by the PCI-DSS Systems Manager Automation remediation documents that AWS Config Conformance Pack remediation actions invoke.
      AssumeRolePolicyDocument:
        Version: '2012-10-17'
        Statement:
          - Sid: AllowSsmEc2AndEventBridgeToAssumeRole
            Effect: Allow
            Principal:
              Service:
                - ssm.amazonaws.com
                - ec2.amazonaws.com
                - events.amazonaws.com
            Action:
              - sts:AssumeRole
      Policies:
        - PolicyName: pci-remediation-actions
          PolicyDocument:
            Version: '2012-10-17'
            Statement:
              - Sid: PciEc2RemediationActions
                Effect: Allow
                Action:
                  - ec2:ReleaseAddress
                  - ec2:DescribeAddresses
                  - ec2:DescribeSecurityGroups
                  - ec2:DeleteSecurityGroup
                  - ec2:RevokeSecurityGroupIngress
                  - ec2:RevokeSecurityGroupEgress
                Resource: '*'
              - Sid: PciAutoScalingRemediationActions
                Effect: Allow
                Action:
                  - autoscaling:DescribeAutoScalingGroups
                  - autoscaling:UpdateAutoScalingGroup
                Resource: '*'
  PCIDefaultSecurityGroupRemediationDocument:
    Type: AWS::SSM::Document
    DeletionPolicy: Retain
    UpdateReplacePolicy: Retain
    Properties:
      Name: pci-default-security-group-restriction-remediation
      DocumentType: Automation
      Content:
        schemaVersion: '0.3'
        description: Revokes all inbound rules (self referencing, IPv4 and IPv6) and all outbound rules from the default security group of the specified VPC so that the VPC default security group no longer allows any traffic.
        parameters:
          AutomationAssumeRole:
            type: String
            description: (Required) The ARN of the IAM role that allows Automation to perform the actions on your behalf.
            default:
              Fn::GetAtt:
                - PCIAutomationAssumeRole
                - Arn
          VpcId:
            type: String
            description: (Required) The ID of the VPC whose default security group is remediated.
        mainSteps:
          - name: describeDefaultSecurityGroup
            action: aws:executeAwsApi
            assumeRole: '{{ AutomationAssumeRole }}'
            inputs:
              Service: ec2
              Api: DescribeSecurityGroups
              Filters:
                - Name: group-name
                  Values:
                    - default
                - Name: vpc-id
                  Values:
                    - '{{ VpcId }}'
            outputs:
              - Name: GroupId
                Selector: '$.SecurityGroups[0].GroupId'
                Type: String
            nextStep: revokeIngressFromSelf
          - name: revokeIngressFromSelf
            action: aws:executeAwsApi
            assumeRole: '{{ AutomationAssumeRole }}'
            onFailure: Continue
            inputs:
              Service: ec2
              Api: RevokeSecurityGroupIngress
              GroupId: '{{ describeDefaultSecurityGroup.GroupId }}'
              IpPermissions:
                - IpProtocol: '-1'
                  UserIdGroupPairs:
                    - GroupId: '{{ describeDefaultSecurityGroup.GroupId }}'
            nextStep: revokeIngressFromIpv4Any
          - name: revokeIngressFromIpv4Any
            action: aws:executeAwsApi
            assumeRole: '{{ AutomationAssumeRole }}'
            onFailure: Continue
            inputs:
              Service: ec2
              Api: RevokeSecurityGroupIngress
              GroupId: '{{ describeDefaultSecurityGroup.GroupId }}'
              IpPermissions:
                - IpProtocol: '-1'
                  IpRanges:
                    - CidrIp: 0.0.0.0/0
            nextStep: revokeIngressFromIpv6Any
          - name: revokeIngressFromIpv6Any
            action: aws:executeAwsApi
            assumeRole: '{{ AutomationAssumeRole }}'
            onFailure: Continue
            inputs:
              Service: ec2
              Api: RevokeSecurityGroupIngress
              GroupId: '{{ describeDefaultSecurityGroup.GroupId }}'
              IpPermissions:
                - IpProtocol: '-1'
                  Ipv6Ranges:
                    - CidrIpv6: '::/0'
            nextStep: revokeEgressToIpv4Any
          - name: revokeEgressToIpv4Any
            action: aws:executeAwsApi
            assumeRole: '{{ AutomationAssumeRole }}'
            onFailure: Continue
            inputs:
              Service: ec2
              Api: RevokeSecurityGroupEgress
              GroupId: '{{ describeDefaultSecurityGroup.GroupId }}'
              IpPermissions:
                - IpProtocol: '-1'
                  IpRanges:
                    - CidrIp: 0.0.0.0/0
            nextStep: revokeEgressToIpv6Any
          - name: revokeEgressToIpv6Any
            action: aws:executeAwsApi
            assumeRole: '{{ AutomationAssumeRole }}'
            onFailure: Continue
            inputs:
              Service: ec2
              Api: RevokeSecurityGroupEgress
              GroupId: '{{ describeDefaultSecurityGroup.GroupId }}'
              IpPermissions:
                - IpProtocol: '-1'
                  Ipv6Ranges:
                    - CidrIpv6: '::/0'
  PCIUnusedSecurityGroupRemediationDocument:
    Type: AWS::SSM::Document
    DeletionPolicy: Retain
    UpdateReplacePolicy: Retain
    Properties:
      Name: pci-unused-security-group-deletion-remediation
      DocumentType: Automation
      Content:
        schemaVersion: '0.3'
        description: Deletes security groups that are not attached to any network interface. The remediation is scoped to the supplied VPC when a VPC ID is provided and to every VPC in the Region otherwise.
        parameters:
          AutomationAssumeRole:
            type: String
            description: (Required) The ARN of the IAM role that allows Automation to perform the actions on your behalf.
            default:
              Fn::GetAtt:
                - PCIAutomationAssumeRole
                - Arn
          VpcId:
            type: String
            description: (Optional) The ID of the VPC to scope the remediation to. Leave empty to evaluate every VPC in the current Region.
            default: ''
        mainSteps:
          - name: chooseSecurityGroupScope
            action: aws:branch
            assumeRole: '{{ AutomationAssumeRole }}'
            inputs:
              Choices:
                - NextStep: describeUnusedSecurityGroupsInVpc
                  Variable: '{{ VpcId }}'
                  StringLike: 'vpc-*'
              Default: describeUnusedSecurityGroupsInAccount
          - name: describeUnusedSecurityGroupsInVpc
            action: aws:executeAwsApi
            assumeRole: '{{ AutomationAssumeRole }}'
            inputs:
              Service: ec2
              Api: DescribeSecurityGroups
              Filters:
                - Name: vpc-id
                  Values:
                    - '{{ VpcId }}'
            outputs:
              - Name: UnusedSecurityGroupIds
                Selector: '$.SecurityGroups[?(@.NetworkInterfaces.length() == 0)].GroupId'
                Type: StringList
            nextStep: deleteUnusedSecurityGroupsInVpc
          - name: deleteUnusedSecurityGroupsInVpc
            action: aws:loop
            assumeRole: '{{ AutomationAssumeRole }}'
            inputs:
              MaxConcurrency: 1
              Iterators: '{{ describeUnusedSecurityGroupsInVpc.UnusedSecurityGroupIds }}'
              Steps:
                - name: deleteSecurityGroupInVpc
                  action: aws:executeAwsApi
                  assumeRole: '{{ AutomationAssumeRole }}'
                  inputs:
                    Service: ec2
                    Api: DeleteSecurityGroup
                    GroupId: '{{ deleteUnusedSecurityGroupsInVpc.CurrentItem }}'
          - name: describeUnusedSecurityGroupsInAccount
            action: aws:executeAwsApi
            assumeRole: '{{ AutomationAssumeRole }}'
            inputs:
              Service: ec2
              Api: DescribeSecurityGroups
            outputs:
              - Name: UnusedSecurityGroupIds
                Selector: '$.SecurityGroups[?(@.NetworkInterfaces.length() == 0)].GroupId'
                Type: StringList
            nextStep: deleteUnusedSecurityGroupsInAccount
          - name: deleteUnusedSecurityGroupsInAccount
            action: aws:loop
            assumeRole: '{{ AutomationAssumeRole }}'
            inputs:
              MaxConcurrency: 1
              Iterators: '{{ describeUnusedSecurityGroupsInAccount.UnusedSecurityGroupIds }}'
              Steps:
                - name: deleteSecurityGroupInAccount
                  action: aws:executeAwsApi
                  assumeRole: '{{ AutomationAssumeRole }}'
                  inputs:
                    Service: ec2
                    Api: DeleteSecurityGroup
                    GroupId: '{{ deleteUnusedSecurityGroupsInAccount.CurrentItem }}'
  PCIUnassociatedElasticIpRemediationDocument:
    Type: AWS::SSM::Document
    DeletionPolicy: Retain
    UpdateReplacePolicy: Retain
    Properties:
      Name: pci-unassociated-elastic-ip-release-remediation
      DocumentType: Automation
      Content:
        schemaVersion: '0.3'
        description: Releases Elastic IP addresses that are not associated with any resource. Only the supplied allocation IDs are evaluated and any address that is still associated is skipped.
        parameters:
          AutomationAssumeRole:
            type: String
            description: (Required) The ARN of the IAM role that allows Automation to perform the actions on your behalf.
            default:
              Fn::GetAtt:
                - PCIAutomationAssumeRole
                - Arn
          AllocationIds:
            type: StringList
            description: (Required) Comma-separated list of Elastic IP allocation IDs (for example eipalloc-0123456789abcdef0) to evaluate and release when they are not associated.
        mainSteps:
          - name: describeAddresses
            action: aws:executeAwsApi
            assumeRole: '{{ AutomationAssumeRole }}'
            inputs:
              Service: ec2
              Api: DescribeAddresses
              AllocationIds: '{{ AllocationIds }}'
            outputs:
              - Name: UnassociatedAllocationIds
                Selector: '$.Addresses[?(@.AssociationId == null)].AllocationId'
                Type: StringList
            nextStep: releaseUnassociatedAddresses
          - name: releaseUnassociatedAddresses
            action: aws:loop
            assumeRole: '{{ AutomationAssumeRole }}'
            inputs:
              MaxConcurrency: 1
              Iterators: '{{ describeAddresses.UnassociatedAllocationIds }}'
              Steps:
                - name: releaseElasticIpAddress
                  action: aws:executeAwsApi
                  assumeRole: '{{ AutomationAssumeRole }}'
                  inputs:
                    Service: ec2
                    Api: ReleaseAddress
                    AllocationId: '{{ releaseUnassociatedAddresses.CurrentItem }}'
  PCIAutoScalingHealthCheckRemediationDocument:
    Type: AWS::SSM::Document
    DeletionPolicy: Retain
    UpdateReplacePolicy: Retain
    Properties:
      Name: pci-autoscaling-health-check-remediation
      DocumentType: Automation
      Content:
        schemaVersion: '0.3'
        description: Updates an Auto Scaling group so that it uses ELB health checks with a health check grace period of 300 seconds.
        parameters:
          AutomationAssumeRole:
            type: String
            description: (Required) The ARN of the IAM role that allows Automation to perform the actions on your behalf.
            default:
              Fn::GetAtt:
                - PCIAutomationAssumeRole
                - Arn
          AutoScalingGroupName:
            type: String
            description: (Required) The name of the Auto Scaling group whose health check configuration is remediated.
        mainSteps:
          - name: describeAutoScalingGroup
            action: aws:executeAwsApi
            assumeRole: '{{ AutomationAssumeRole }}'
            inputs:
              Service: autoscaling
              Api: DescribeAutoScalingGroups
              AutoScalingGroupNames:
                - '{{ AutoScalingGroupName }}'
            outputs:
              - Name: AutoScalingGroupName
                Selector: '$.AutoScalingGroups[0].AutoScalingGroupName'
                Type: String
            nextStep: updateAutoScalingGroupHealthCheck
          - name: updateAutoScalingGroupHealthCheck
            action: aws:executeAwsApi
            assumeRole: '{{ AutomationAssumeRole }}'
            inputs:
              Service: autoscaling
              Api: UpdateAutoScalingGroup
              AutoScalingGroupName: '{{ describeAutoScalingGroup.AutoScalingGroupName }}'
              HealthCheckType: ELB
              HealthCheckGracePeriod: 300
Outputs:
  PCIAutomationAssumeRoleArn:
    Description: ARN of the shared IAM role assumed by the PCI-DSS remediation Automation documents.
    Value:
      Fn::GetAtt:
        - PCIAutomationAssumeRole
        - Arn
  PCIAutomationAssumeRoleName:
    Description: Name of the shared IAM role assumed by the PCI-DSS remediation Automation documents.
    Value:
      Ref: PCIAutomationAssumeRole
  DefaultSecurityGroupRemediationDocumentName:
    Description: Name of the SSM Automation document that revokes all ingress and egress rules from a VPC default security group.
    Value:
      Ref: PCIDefaultSecurityGroupRemediationDocument
  UnusedSecurityGroupRemediationDocumentName:
    Description: Name of the SSM Automation document that deletes unused security groups.
    Value:
      Ref: PCIUnusedSecurityGroupRemediationDocument
  UnassociatedElasticIpRemediationDocumentName:
    Description: Name of the SSM Automation document that releases unassociated Elastic IP addresses by allocation ID.
    Value:
      Ref: PCIUnassociatedElasticIpRemediationDocument
  AutoScalingHealthCheckRemediationDocumentName:
    Description: Name of the SSM Automation document that sets an Auto Scaling group's health check type to ELB with a 300 second grace period.
    Value:
      Ref: PCIAutoScalingHealthCheckRemediationDocument

AWSTemplateFormatVersion: '2010-09-09'
Description: >-
  Ear Hustle production DNS. Creates the Route53 public hosted zone for the
  application domain together with every production DNS record: apex SPF,
  Google site verification, Zoom verification, DMARC and ATProto TXT records,
  Google Workspace MX (apex and legacy subdomain) and DKIM, Squarespace A and
  CNAME records, podcast feed and Supercast CNAME records, ZenDesk verification,
  domain validation and DKIM records, Campaign Monitor DKIM, SPF and MX records,
  plus an ACM certificate for the podcast feeds subdomain validated with DNS.

Parameters:

  DomainName:
    Type: String
    Default: earhustlesq.com
    AllowedPattern: '^([a-zA-Z0-9]([a-zA-Z0-9\-]{0,61}[a-zA-Z0-9])?\.)+[a-zA-Z]{2,}$'
    ConstraintDescription: Must be a valid DNS domain name, for example earhustlesq.com.
    Description: >-
      Apex domain name for the hosted zone. All subdomain records are created
      as children of this name.

  OldSubdomainName:
    Type: String
    Default: old
    AllowedPattern: '^[a-zA-Z0-9]([a-zA-Z0-9\-]{0,61}[a-zA-Z0-9])?$'
    ConstraintDescription: Must be a valid DNS label, for example old.
    Description: >-
      Legacy subdomain (relative label, without the domain suffix) that also
      receives the Google Workspace MX records.

  SpfRecordValue:
    Type: String
    Default: 'v=spf1 include:_spf.google.com include:cmail1.com include:servers.mcsv.net include:spf.supercast.com ~all'
    Description: >-
      Full SPF policy string published as a TXT record at the domain apex
      (Google Workspace, Campaign Monitor, Mailchimp and Supercast senders).

  GoogleSiteVerificationToken:
    Type: String
    NoEcho: true
    Default: REPLACE_WITH_GOOGLE_SITE_VERIFICATION_TOKEN
    Description: >-
      Google Search Console site verification token (the value after
      google-site-verification=). Placeholder default: override with the real
      production token at deploy time.

  ZoomVerificationToken:
    Type: String
    NoEcho: true
    Default: REPLACE_WITH_ZOOM_VERIFICATION_TOKEN
    Description: >-
      Zoom domain verification token (the value after zoom-verification=).
      Placeholder default: override with the real production token at deploy
      time.

  DmarcEmail:
    Type: String
    Default: dmarc@earhustlesq.com
    AllowedPattern: '^[^@\s]+@[^@\s]+\.[a-zA-Z]{2,}$'
    ConstraintDescription: Must be a valid email address.
    Description: Email address that receives DMARC aggregate reports (rua).

  AtProtoDid:
    Type: String
    Default: 'did:plc:REPLACE_WITH_ATPROTO_DID'
    Description: >-
      ATProto decentralized identifier published at _atproto, for example
      did:plc:xxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxx or did:web:earhustlesq.com. Placeholder
      default: override with the real production DID at deploy time.

  GoogleWorkspaceDkimPublicKey:
    Type: String
    NoEcho: true
    Default: REPLACE_WITH_GOOGLE_WORKSPACE_DKIM_PUBLIC_KEY
    Description: >-
      Google Workspace DKIM public key published at google._domainkey
      (the value after "v=DKIM1; k=rsa; p="). Placeholder default: override with
      the real production public key at deploy time.

  SquarespaceVerificationName:
    Type: String
    Default: sqsp-verification
    AllowedPattern: '^[a-zA-Z0-9]([a-zA-Z0-9\-]{0,61}[a-zA-Z0-9])?$'
    ConstraintDescription: Must be a valid DNS label, for example the verification host shown by Squarespace.
    Description: >-
      Host label (relative, without the domain suffix) used for the Squarespace
      domain verification CNAME. Placeholder default: override with the real
      verification label at deploy time.

  SquarespaceVerificationTarget:
    Type: String
    Default: verification.squarespace.com
    Description: >-
      Target hostname provided by Squarespace for domain verification.
      Placeholder default: override with the real target at deploy time.

  WwwTarget:
    Type: String
    Default: ext-sq.squarespace.com
    Description: Squarespace target hostname for the www CNAME record.

  FeedsTarget:
    Type: String
    Default: cname.supercast.com
    Description: Supercast target hostname for the podcast feeds CNAME record.

  SupercastDkimTarget:
    Type: String
    Default: supercast._domainkey.supercast.com
    Description: >-
      Supercast target hostname for the DKIM CNAME record at
      supercast._domainkey. Placeholder default: override with the real target
      at deploy time.

  SupercastReturnPathTarget:
    Type: String
    Default: rp.supercast.com
    Description: >-
      Supercast target hostname for the return-path CNAME record at rp.
      Placeholder default: override with the real target at deploy time.

  ZenDeskVerificationName:
    Type: String
    Default: zendeskverification
    AllowedPattern: '^[a-zA-Z0-9]([a-zA-Z0-9\-]{0,61}[a-zA-Z0-9])?$'
    ConstraintDescription: Must be a valid DNS label.
    Description: Host label (relative, without the domain suffix) for the ZenDesk TXT verification record.

  ZenDeskVerificationToken:
    Type: String
    NoEcho: true
    Default: REPLACE_WITH_ZENDESK_VERIFICATION_TOKEN
    Description: >-
      ZenDesk verification token published as a TXT record. Placeholder default:
      override with the real production token at deploy time.

  ZenDeskSubdomain:
    Type: String
    Default: support
    AllowedPattern: '^[a-zA-Z0-9]([a-zA-Z0-9\-]{0,61}[a-zA-Z0-9])?$'
    ConstraintDescription: Must be a valid DNS label, for example support.
    Description: >-
      ZenDesk subdomain used both as the label of the domain validation CNAME
      and as the ZenDesk hostname prefix.

  ZenDeskDkim1Target:
    Type: String
    Default: zendesk1.domainkey.zendesk.com
    Description: ZenDesk target hostname for the first DKIM CNAME record (zendesk1._domainkey).

  ZenDeskDkim2Target:
    Type: String
    Default: zendesk2.domainkey.zendesk.com
    Description: ZenDesk target hostname for the second DKIM CNAME record (zendesk2._domainkey).

  CampaignMonitorDkimTarget:
    Type: String
    Default: cm._domainkey.cmail1.com
    Description: >-
      Campaign Monitor target hostname for the DKIM CNAME record at
      cm._domainkey. Placeholder default: override with the real target at
      deploy time.

Resources:

  HostedZone:
    Type: AWS::Route53::HostedZone
    DeletionPolicy: Retain
    UpdateReplacePolicy: Retain
    Properties:
      Name: !Ref DomainName
      HostedZoneConfig:
        Comment: !Sub 'Ear Hustle production DNS zone for ${DomainName}'
      HostedZoneTags:
        - Key: 'prx:ops:environment'
          Value: 'Production'
        - Key: 'prx:dev:application'
          Value: 'Ear Hustle'

  # Apex TXT records: SPF, Google site verification and Zoom verification are
  # published as a single TXT record set because Route 53 allows only one TXT
  # record set per DNS name.
  ApexTxtRecords:
    Type: AWS::Route53::RecordSet
    Properties:
      HostedZoneId: !Ref HostedZone
      Name: !Ref DomainName
      Type: TXT
      TTL: '300'
      ResourceRecords:
        - !Sub '"${SpfRecordValue}"'
        - !Sub '"google-site-verification=${GoogleSiteVerificationToken}"'
        - !Sub '"zoom-verification=${ZoomVerificationToken}"'

  DmarcRecord:
    Type: AWS::Route53::RecordSet
    Properties:
      HostedZoneId: !Ref HostedZone
      Name: !Sub '_dmarc.${DomainName}'
      Type: TXT
      TTL: '300'
      ResourceRecords:
        - !Sub '"v=DMARC1; p=none; rua=mailto:${DmarcEmail}"'

  AtProtoRecord:
    Type: AWS::Route53::RecordSet
    Properties:
      HostedZoneId: !Ref HostedZone
      Name: !Sub '_atproto.${DomainName}'
      Type: TXT
      TTL: '300'
      ResourceRecords:
        - !Sub '"did=${AtProtoDid}"'

  ApexMxRecords:
    Type: AWS::Route53::RecordSet
    Properties:
      HostedZoneId: !Ref HostedZone
      Name: !Ref DomainName
      Type: MX
      TTL: '3600'
      ResourceRecords:
        - '1 ASPMX.L.GOOGLE.COM'
        - '5 ALT1.ASPMX.L.GOOGLE.COM'
        - '5 ALT2.ASPMX.L.GOOGLE.COM'
        - '10 ALT3.ASPMX.L.GOOGLE.COM'
        - '10 ALT4.ASPMX.L.GOOGLE.COM'

  OldSubdomainMxRecords:
    Type: AWS::Route53::RecordSet
    Properties:
      HostedZoneId: !Ref HostedZone
      Name: !Sub '${OldSubdomainName}.${DomainName}'
      Type: MX
      TTL: '3600'
      ResourceRecords:
        - '1 ASPMX.L.GOOGLE.COM'
        - '5 ALT1.ASPMX.L.GOOGLE.COM'
        - '5 ALT2.ASPMX.L.GOOGLE.COM'
        - '10 ALT3.ASPMX.L.GOOGLE.COM'
        - '10 ALT4.ASPMX.L.GOOGLE.COM'

  ApexARecords:
    Type: AWS::Route53::RecordSet
    Properties:
      HostedZoneId: !Ref HostedZone
      Name: !Ref DomainName
      Type: A
      TTL: '3600'
      ResourceRecords:
        - '198.185.159.144'
        - '198.185.159.145'
        - '198.49.23.144'
        - '198.49.23.145'

  WwwCnameRecord:
    Type: AWS::Route53::RecordSet
    Properties:
      HostedZoneId: !Ref HostedZone
      Name: !Sub 'www.${DomainName}'
      Type: CNAME
      TTL: '300'
      ResourceRecords:
        - !Ref WwwTarget

  FeedsCnameRecord:
    Type: AWS::Route53::RecordSet
    Properties:
      HostedZoneId: !Ref HostedZone
      Name: !Sub 'feeds.${DomainName}'
      Type: CNAME
      TTL: '300'
      ResourceRecords:
        - !Ref FeedsTarget

  SquarespaceVerificationRecord:
    Type: AWS::Route53::RecordSet
    Properties:
      HostedZoneId: !Ref HostedZone
      Name: !Sub '${SquarespaceVerificationName}.${DomainName}'
      Type: CNAME
      TTL: '300'
      ResourceRecords:
        - !Ref SquarespaceVerificationTarget

  ZenDeskVerificationRecord:

AWSTemplateFormatVersion: '2010-09-09'
Description: >-
  Multi-tenant QuickSight dashboard application on AWS App Runner. This template
  is fully self-contained: it creates the Amazon ECR repository that hosts the
  container image, the App Runner ECR access ("build") role, the App Runner
  task/instance role with Directory Service and QuickSight tenant-provisioning
  permissions, and the App Runner service itself with auto-deployments enabled,
  an HTTP health check on /status at container port 8080, and the QuickSight
  runtime environment configuration. No external VPC, subnet, security group,
  AMI, key pair, secret, SSM parameter, exported value, or hardcoded ARN is
  referenced.
  Note: App Runner ingress NetworkConfiguration and ObservabilityConfiguration
  are intentionally omitted; the public endpoint is used and managed by App
  Runner. No unverified sub-properties are invented.

Parameters:
  ImageTag:
    Type: String
    Description: >-
      Container image tag in the ECR repository that App Runner deploys and
      tracks for auto-deployments. The repository uses IMMUTABLE image tags, so
      each build/release MUST supply a distinct, never-reused tag (for example a
      semantic version such as 1.2.0 or a commit SHA); re-pushing an existing tag
      will be rejected by Amazon ECR. Override this default per release.
    Default: '1.0.0'
    MinLength: 1
    MaxLength: 128
    AllowedPattern: '^[a-zA-Z0-9][a-zA-Z0-9._-]*$'
    ConstraintDescription: Must be a valid Amazon ECR image tag.

Resources:

  # ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
  # Container image registry for the multi-tenant QuickSight dashboard
  # ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
  DashboardRepository:
    Type: AWS::ECR::Repository
    Properties:
      RepositoryName: quicksight-multitenant-dashboard
      ImageTagMutability: IMMUTABLE
      ImageScanningConfiguration:
        ScanOnPush: true
      EncryptionConfiguration:
        EncryptionType: AES256
      Tags:
        - Key: Name
          Value: quicksight-multitenant-dashboard

  # ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
  # App Runner "build" role - assumed by App Runner to pull the image from ECR
  # ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
  AppRunnerEcrAccessRole:
    Type: AWS::IAM::Role
    Properties:
      RoleName: quicksight-multitenant-apprunner-ecr-access
      Description: App Runner build role granting access to pull the dashboard image from Amazon ECR.
      AssumeRolePolicyDocument:
        Version: '2012-10-17'
        Statement:
          - Sid: AllowAppRunnerBuildToAssumeRole
            Effect: Allow
            Principal:
              Service: build.apprunner.amazonaws.com
            Action: sts:AssumeRole
      ManagedPolicyArns:
        - !Sub 'arn:${AWS::Partition}:iam::aws:policy/service-role/AWSAppRunnerServicePolicyForECRAccess'
      Policies:
        - PolicyName: EcrImagePullAccess
          PolicyDocument:
            Version: '2012-10-17'
            Statement:
              - Sid: AllowEcrAuthorizationToken
                Effect: Allow
                Action:
                  - ecr:GetAuthorizationToken
                Resource: '*'
              - Sid: AllowImagePullFromDashboardRepository
                Effect: Allow
                Action:
                  - ecr:BatchCheckLayerAvailability
                  - ecr:BatchGetImage
                  - ecr:GetDownloadUrlForLayer
                  - ecr:DescribeImages
                  - ecr:DescribeRepositories
                  - ecr:ListImages
                Resource: !GetAtt DashboardRepository.Arn
      Tags:
        - Key: Name
          Value: quicksight-multitenant-apprunner-ecr-access

  # ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
  # App Runner task/instance role - Directory Service + QuickSight provisioning
  # ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
  AppRunnerTaskRole:
    Type: AWS::IAM::Role
    Properties:
      RoleName: quicksight-multitenant-apprunner-task
      Description: App Runner task role granting Directory Service and QuickSight permissions used for multi-tenant provisioning.
      AssumeRolePolicyDocument:
        Version: '2012-10-17'
        Statement:
          - Sid: AllowAppRunnerTasksToAssumeRole
            Effect: Allow
            Principal:
              Service: tasks.apprunner.amazonaws.com
            Action: sts:AssumeRole
      Policies:
        - PolicyName: DirectoryServiceTenantProvisioning
          PolicyDocument:
            Version: '2012-10-17'
            Statement:
              - Sid: DirectoryServiceProvisioning
                Effect: Allow
                Action:
                  - ds:CreateDirectory
                  - ds:CreateMicrosoftAD
                  - ds:CreateNamespace
                  - ds:CreateTrust
                  - ds:RegisterCertificate
                  - ds:VerifyTrust
                  - ds:DescribeDirectories
                  - ds:DescribeTrusts
                  - ds:DescribeCertificate
                  - ds:ListCertificates
                  - ds:*Directory*
                Resource: '*'
        - PolicyName: QuickSightTenantProvisioning
          PolicyDocument:
            Version: '2012-10-17'
            Statement:
              - Sid: QuickSightProvisioning
                Effect: Allow
                Action:
                  - quicksight:CreateNamespace
                  - quicksight:CreateDataSet
                  - quicksight:CreateDataSource
                  - quicksight:CreateTemplate
                  - quicksight:RegisterUser
                  - quicksight:Describe*
                  - quicksight:List*
                  - quicksight:Update*
                  - quicksight:TagResource
                  - quicksight:PassDataSet
                Resource: '*'
      Tags:
        - Key: Name
          Value: quicksight-multitenant-apprunner-task

  # ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
  # App Runner service for the multi-tenant QuickSight dashboard
  # ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
  DashboardService:
    Type: AWS::AppRunner::Service
    Properties:
      ServiceName: quicksight-multitenant-dashboard
      SourceConfiguration:
        AutoDeploymentsEnabled: true
        AuthenticationConfiguration:
          AccessRoleArn: !GetAtt AppRunnerEcrAccessRole.Arn
        ImageRepository:
          ImageIdentifier: !Sub '${DashboardRepository.RepositoryUri}:${ImageTag}'
          ImageRepositoryType: ECR
          ImageConfiguration:
            Port: '8080'
            RuntimeEnvironmentVariables:
              - Name: ALLOW_IP_RANGE
                Value: '0.0.0.0/0'
              - Name: AWS_REGION
                Value: !Ref AWS::Region
              - Name: AWS_ACCOUNT_ID
                Value: !Ref AWS::AccountId
              - Name: EMAIL
                Value: 'admin@example.com'
              - Name: ADMIN_USER
                Value: 'admin'
              - Name: QS_TEMPLATE_ID
                Value: 'quicksight-multitenant-template'
              - Name: QS_DATASET_ID
                Value: 'quicksight-multitenant-dataset'
              - Name: QS_DATASOURCE_ID
                Value: 'quicksight-multitenant-datasource'
              - Name: QS_DATABASE
                Value: 'quicksight_multitenant_db'
              - Name: QS_TABLE
                Value: 'tenant_dashboard'
              - Name: QS_FILTER_COLUMN
                Value: 'tenant_id'
      InstanceConfiguration:
        Cpu: '1024'
        Memory: '2048'
        InstanceRoleArn: !GetAtt AppRunnerTaskRole.Arn
      HealthCheckConfiguration:
        Protocol: HTTP
        Path: /status
        Interval: 10
        Timeout: 5
        HealthyThreshold: 1
        UnhealthyThreshold: 5
      Tags:
        - Key: Name
          Value: quicksight-multitenant-dashboard

Outputs:
  ContainerImageUri:
    Description: Fully qualified ECR image URI that the App Runner service deploys.
    Value: !Sub '${DashboardRepository.RepositoryUri}:${ImageTag}'
    Export:
      Name: !Sub '${AWS::StackName}-ContainerImageUri'

  RepositoryUri:
    Description: URI of the Amazon ECR repository that hosts the dashboard container image.
    Value: !GetAtt DashboardRepository.RepositoryUri
    Export:
      Name: !Sub '${AWS::StackName}-RepositoryUri'

  ServiceUrl:
    Description: Public HTTPS URL of the App Runner service hosting the multi-tenant QuickSight dashboard.
    Value: !GetAtt DashboardService.ServiceUrl
    Export:
      Name: !Sub '${AWS::StackName}-ServiceUrl'
